summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Australia posted 260/10 (94.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 105/10 (40.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Steve O'Keefe (6/35), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Steve O'Keefe delivered a masterclass for Australia (6 Runs & 12 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 49%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, India faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by R Ashwin (9 Runs & 7 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by 333 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While India produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
